span.label: existence
span.quote: Experiments 1 and 3, contrary to most recent accounts of visual masking, seem to imply that a word which is backward pattern masked such that it is not only unreportable but also undetectable, nevertheless gains access to a lexical or semantic representation.

span.label: semantic processing of pattern-masked words without awareness
span.quote: What has been shown is that words have been analyzed to a lexical if not semantic level without awareness.

span.quote: The object of the first study was to obtain comparative estimates of the availability and usability of three aspects of word stimuli over a range of stimulus-mask onset asynchronies.

span.quote: Of course these sorts of general statements rely on an assumed equivalence of scaling of graphic and semantic similarity in the present experiments.

span.label: iconic memory
span.quote: The currently held interpretation of masking (Sperling, 1967; Turvey, 1973) is that it disrupts a relatively raw representation of visual input (iconic memory), without which input cannot be processed to achieve semantic or phonological coding.

span.label: Central Masking
span.quote: Several characteristics distinguish Peripheral and Central Masking. Central Masking can only be obtained with a contour pattern, can only be obtained effectively by the mask following the target (backward masking), is possible both monoptically and dichoptically, and is characterized by an onset-onset function. Peripheral masking is obtainable with a blank field, a noise field, or a contoured field, works in both forward and backward directions, cannot be obtained dichoptically, and is characterized by an energy function.

span.label: Peripheral masking
span.quote: Several characteristics distinguish Peripheral and Central Masking. Central Masking can only be obtained with a contour pattern, can only be obtained effectively by the mask following the target (backward masking), is possible both monoptically and dichoptically, and is characterized by an onset-onset function. Peripheral masking is obtainable with a blank field, a noise field, or a contoured field, works in both forward and backward directions, cannot be obtained dichoptically, and is characterized by an energy function.

span.label: **THE ORDERING RESULT, AND IT RUNS THE WRONG WAY FOR THE STANDARD ACCOUNT:** `As SOA is reduced, DETECTION judgments suffer first, GRAPHIC similarity judgments fall next, and SEMANTIC judgments fall last.` The received view was that masking interrupts the icon and that without the icon there is nothing left to analyse for meaning - which predicts semantic judgments failing first, or at latest with the rest. **They are the most robust of the three.** Three measures, one manipulation, a fixed order, and the order is the argument
span.quote: As SOA is reduced, detection judgments suffer first, graphic similarity judgments fall next, and semantic judgments fall last.

span.label: **AND THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT A DISSOCIATION RATHER THAN A FAILED MASK:** `while NO SUBJECT WAS AWARE of the first letter string under EITHER masking condition, all subjects showed a substantial advantage for associated words when the first was CENTRALLY masked while NONE did when it was PERIPHERALLY masked.` `They could not see it and were primed anyway` invites `then your mask did not work`. **Marcel's reply is a second mask that also abolishes awareness and also abolishes the priming** - awareness held constant at zero, priming moved from 56 msec to 4. Compare erb2019 and eckstein2007 in this corpus: the same manoeuvre, thirty years later, still being reinvented
span.quote: while no subject was aware of the first letter string under either masking condition, all subjects showed a substantial advantage for associated words when the first was centrally masked while none did when it was peripherally masked.

span.label: **THE POSITION BEING OVERTURNED, STATED IN ITS OWN WORDS BEFORE IT IS DISMANTLED:** `The currently held interpretation of masking (Sperling, 1967; Turvey, 1973) is that it disrupts a relatively raw representation of visual input (ICONIC MEMORY), WITHOUT WHICH input cannot be processed to achieve semantic or phonological coding.` Worth holding as a record of what the field believed in 1983, and worth marking as a view the paper REJECTS - a triple built from this sentence would enter the graph asserting the opposite of the record's finding, which is the fault I dropped an edge for on eckstein2007 this afternoon
span.quote: The currently held interpretation of masking (Sperling, 1967; Turvey, 1973) is that it disrupts a relatively raw representation of visual input (iconic memory), without which input cannot be processed to achieve semantic or phonological coding.

span.label: `Central Masking` / `Peripheral masking` - DISTINGUISHED BY AN ENUMERATION OF PROPERTIES, NOT BY A DEFINITION. `SEVERAL CHARACTERISTICS DISTINGUISH Peripheral and Central Masking` - then four contrasts run in parallel across the two, and the pair is never given a mechanism. The dichoptic test is the one that separates them cleanly: Central `is possible both monoptically and dichoptically`, Peripheral `CANNOT BE OBTAINED DICHOPTICALLY`.
span.quote: Several characteristics distinguish Peripheral and Central Masking. Central Masking can only be obtained with a contour pattern, can only be obtained effectively by the mask following the target (backward masking), is possible both monoptically and dichoptically, and is characterized by an onset-onset function. Peripheral masking is obtainable with a blank field, a noise field, or a contoured field, works in both forward and backward directions, cannot be obtained dichoptically, and is characterized by an energy function.

span.label: `pattern-masking` / `energy-masking` - TWO PROCEDURES THAT ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, AND THE PAPER USES THE DIFFERENCE TO EXPLAIN A LITERATURE. `the PATTERN-MASKING procedure employed here OPERATES BY SOA, IN CONTRAST TO the ENERGY-MASKING procedure, which DOES WORK BY ENERGY AND FAILS TO PRODUCE UNCONSCIOUS PRIMING EFFECTS`. The second clause is a NULL RESULT about a method, which is why the edge below is a contrast and not a causal claim.
span.quote: the pattern-masking procedure employed here operates by SOA, in contrast to the energy-masking procedure, which does work by energy and fails to produce unconscious priming effects

span.label: extends → Wickens (1972)
span.quote: However, the results bear out and add to his conclusion that semantic information was available when visual information was not.

span.quote: Firstly it both qualifies and extends Turvey’s (1973) distinction between Peripheral and Central Masking.

span.label: contradicts → Shallice (1972) and Morton (1970, 1979a)
span.quote: This is a quite different conception from that of Shallice (1972) and Morton (1970, 1979a).

span.label: detection —distinct-from→ semantic judgments
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — **A DISSOCIATION STATED AS AN ORDERING, WHICH IS STRONGER THAN A DIFFERENCE.** Not `semantic judgments were better` - a fixed sequence in which the three measures fail as one parameter is turned down. Weight 0.95: both endpoints are named as words, the sentence is a result rather than a framing, and the relation asserted is exactly distinctness - if detection and semantic judgment drew on one representation they could not come apart in a repeatable order. **This is the rare case where the sentence carrying the mechanism also carries the edge** (Q-790), and it does so because the author chose to state the finding as a list of three named measures.
span.quote: As SOA is reduced, detection judgments suffer first, graphic similarity judgments fall next, and semantic judgments fall last.

span.label: Central Masking —distinct-from→ Peripheral masking
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — `Several characteristics distinguish` - asserted outright and then itemised four ways, so weight 1.0.
span.quote: Several characteristics distinguish Peripheral and Central Masking. Central Masking can only be obtained with a contour pattern, can only be obtained effectively by the mask following the target (backward masking), is possible both monoptically and dichoptically, and is characterized by an onset-onset function. Peripheral masking is obtainable with a blank field, a noise field, or a contoured field, works in both forward and backward directions, cannot be obtained dichoptically, and is characterized by an energy function.

span.label: pattern-masking —contrasted-with→ energy-masking
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — NOT typed `causes`. The clause about energy-masking is a FAILURE to produce an effect - `fails to produce unconscious priming effects` - and a null result is not a causal relation. The contrast is what the paper asserts; the null sits in this note where it cannot be read as a mechanism.
